Definition: {properly, a split, i.e. a wide level valley between mountains}
BiblicalUsage: A plain is a wide valley between mountains, and this Aramaic word appears once, in the setting of the golden image. In Daniel 3:1 Nebuchadnezzar set up the image in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon. A wide, flat place, chosen so that everyone could see the idol.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the plain of Dura is the point: idolatry loves an open space where everyone can see it and no one can hide from it.
